description:
Redwood Inference is building a “Shadow Traffic” capability inside its unified rollouts / A/B testing and model lifecycle tooling to evaluate candidate models and configuration changes using production-shaped traffic **without impacting end-user responses**. The project adds a shadow execution path that mirrors a sampled subset of live requests to one or more “shadow targets” (model/version/quantization profile/prompt config), runs them asynchronously, and records quality + performance metrics for analysis and automated rollout guardrails.

Goals:
- Enable per-route, policy-controlled shadowing (sampling %, customer allowlist, region, model target) that never blocks or alters the primary response.
- Capture evaluation metrics suitable for release gating: output similarity/format adherence, safety policy outcomes, LLM-as-judge preference scores, task-specific rubric scores (where configured), plus latency/cost deltas.
- Integrate metrics into Redwood Console dashboards and alerts, and allow rollout policies to reference quality thresholds (e.g., “halt canary if judge win-rate drops > X%”).
- Provide strict operational controls: kill-switch, rate limits, capacity budgets, metric-cardinality guardrails, and clear SLO impact boundaries.
- Meet security/compliance expectations: configurable retention, payload redaction, and customer controls for data residency and logging.

Non-goals:
- Replacing offline benchmark suites; this complements eval-harness by providing production-like sampling.
- Perfect “ground truth” correctness for all tasks; the system focuses on repeatable comparative signals and regression detection.

Key stakeholders:
- Product: Marissa Cole (Console & Rollouts), Paula Mendes (rollout policies/telemetry requirements)
- Engineering (Console & Tooling / Platform): Dylan Brooks, Chloe Martin, Jada Williams, Jin Woo Park
- Telemetry & Analytics: Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman, Caleb Johnson, Mei Lin
- Smart Routing / Policy Engine: Mina Haddad, Ravi Menon, Jordan Lee, Benji Okafor
- Applied ML / Evals: Jonas Weber, Selene Huang, Olivia Grant, Sana Farid
- SRE/Observability: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Allison Grant
- Security & Compliance: Naomi Feldman

High-level timeline (approx. 10–12 weeks):
1) Design + ADRs (weeks 1–2): request mirroring approach, policy schema, retention/redaction, SLO budgets.
2) MVP implementation (weeks 3–6): shadow runner, async queue, metrics emission, basic judge scoring integration.
3) Console + guardrails (weeks 7–9): dashboards, comparisons, alerts, kill switch, cardinality controls.
4) Beta + GA readiness (weeks 10–12): load tests, incident playbooks, documentation, pricing/quotas, staged rollout to select enterprise accounts.

Deliverables:
- Control-plane schema + policy engine support for shadow targets and sampling.
- Data-plane component (“shadow runner”) with strict isolation from primary path.
- Telemetry schema, pipelines, and dashboards.
- Applied-ML scoring configuration and LLM-as-judge guidance.
- Operational playbooks, SLO impact analysis, and security retention policy updates.

files.description: PRD for Shadow Traffic eval metrics: customer problems, personas, success metrics, beta/GA criteria, scoping decisions, and integration with rollouts/A-B testing.
End-to-end design spec: request mirroring, async execution, shadow target selection, linking primary<->shadow via request_id, and failure/timeout behaviors.
ADR comparing approaches (gateway fan-out vs runtime sidecar vs queue-based replay), with chosen design, tradeoffs, and rollback plan.
Metrics schema: event types, required dimensions, allowed tags, cardinality limits, and naming conventions for shadow_eval.* signals.
Service overview for the shadow runner: components, ownership, dependencies, configuration knobs, and operational limits.
Guidelines for LLM-as-judge scoring used in shadow runs: rubric templates, prompt patterns, calibration approach, and known failure modes.
SLO impact analysis: strict requirement that primary p99 latency is unchanged; capacity budgets, rate limiting strategy, and alert thresholds.
Restricted policy update: what shadow payload/outputs can be stored, default retention, redaction rules, residency constraints, and customer opt-out controls.
Runbook for disabling shadow traffic quickly: kill switch paths, safe rollback steps, verification queries/dashboards, and comms checklist.
Postmortem for a beta incident where shadow sampling misconfiguration caused elevated GPU utilization; includes timeline, root cause, mitigations, and follow-ups.
Kickoff notes doc: attendees, initial requirements, open questions (sampling, linking, UI), and early task breakdown.
Working notes on how RoutePolicy/Policy Engine will express shadow targets, sampling, allowlists, and safe defaults.
Telemetry working doc reviewing metric dimensions and cardinality risks; includes proposed tag allowlists and aggregation strategy.
Applied ML scratchpad of judge prompt variants, calibration experiments, and early correlations vs offline benchmarks.
Sheet-style doc: load test matrix (sampling %, concurrency, regions), expected utilization, pass/fail criteria, and results table.
PM/Design collaboration notes: dashboard information architecture, comparison views, and customer-facing terminology.
Release checklist for beta: gating tests, rollout order by region, observability prerequisites, and rollback steps.
Security review notes: data classification, logging policy, retention defaults, access controls, and audit considerations.
Implement shadow runner execution path in data plane (async, isolated from primary response); includes acceptance criteria and perf constraints.
Add shadow sampling + target config to RoutePolicy schema; validation rules, migrations, and safe default behavior.
Telemetry pipeline work: persist shadow run events, join with primary request metadata, and publish aggregated metrics tables.
Console backend: APIs for querying shadow metrics by route/model/region/time window; pagination and permission checks.
Console UI: Shadow evaluation dashboard MVP (time-series, breakdowns, filters) and beta feature-flagging.
Implement cardinality guardrails (tag allowlists, bucketing) for shadow_eval metrics; includes load testing and backpressure behavior.
SRE task: define capacity budget and load test plan; establish alerts (queue depth, shadow error rate) and runbook readiness.
Add global kill switch + per-route disable controls for shadow traffic; ensure can be toggled without deploy.
Eval-harness integration: add LLM-as-judge scorer module and configuration model for shadow runs.
Beta plan and GA criteria: target accounts, success metrics, risk register, and customer communication plan.
Pricing/packaging proposal: quotas for shadow sampling, retention tiers, and cost attribution in billing/analytics.
Design exploration ticket: dashboard layout, comparison visualization, and copywriting for “Shadow Evals” feature.
PR: introduce shadow runner worker and request mirroring hooks; async execution and basic instrumentation.
PR: extend RouteConfig/Policy schema with shadow_traffic fields; add server-side validation and migrations.
PR: emit shadow_eval events/metrics to telemetry pipeline; include request_id linking and sampling metadata.
PR: implement rate limiting + queue backpressure for shadow executions to enforce capacity budgets.
PR: payload redaction and logging controls for shadow traffic (PII filters, config-driven allowlists).
PR: add kill switch and admin override endpoints; integrate with Console admin controls.
PR: Console backend endpoints for shadow metrics queries and aggregated breakdowns.
PR: Console UI for Shadow Evals dashboard (MVP): charts, filters, and beta flag wiring.
PR: rollout policy integration—allow canary/A-B experiments to reference shadow quality gates for automated rollback/hold.
PR: add alert rules and dashboards references for shadow runner error rate, queue depth, and drop counts.
PR (hotfix): fix memory leak / worker lifecycle bug discovered during beta load tests; includes regression test.
PR: LLM-as-judge scorer v1 (rubric prompts, normalization, statistical reporting) used by shadow traffic evaluations.
PR: add Grafana dashboard panels for shadow_eval metrics and SRE overview dashboard wiring.
PR: new perf canary to ensure shadow feature introduces no primary-path latency regression beyond budget.
PR: internal documentation updates for enabling shadow traffic, interpreting metrics, and beta limitations.
